draft.title: Area of rectangles, triangles and parallelograms
card: Area is the amount of flat space inside a shape. It is measured in square units, such as square centimetres (\(\text{cm}^{2}\)).
Area is length times width: \(A = l \times w\). A rectangle 8 cm long and 5 cm wide has area \(8 \times 5 = 40\ \text{cm}^{2}\).
Area is base times perpendicular height: \(A = b \times h\). The height is measured at right angles to the base, not along the slanted side.
Area is half of base times perpendicular height: \(A = \frac{1}{2} \times b \times h\). With base 10 cm and height 6 cm, \(A = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 6 = 30\ \text{cm}^{2}\).
draft.remember: Use the perpendicular height. A triangle is half of base times height.

a.q: A triangle has a base of 12 cm and a perpendicular height of 5 cm. What is its area?
a.why: \(A = \frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 5 = 30\ \text{cm}^{2}\). The answer \(60\ \text{cm}^{2}\) is tempting, but it leaves out the half.
a.clue: Multiply base by height, then take half.

b.q: A parallelogram-shaped garden bed has a base of 9 m. Its slanted side is 6 m and its perpendicular height is 4 m. What is its area?
b.why: Area is base times perpendicular height: \(9 \times 4 = 36\ \text{m}^{2}\). The slanted side of 6 m is not the height, so \(9 \times 6 = 54\) is wrong.
b.clue: Which length meets the base at a right angle?

wants.brief: A parallelogram with base b along the bottom, a slanted side, and a dashed vertical line from the top edge down to the base marked with a right angle and labelled perpendicular height h.
wants.why: It shows that the height is measured at right angles to the base, not along the slanted side.
